From the diff, `embed_category` default is '' (site_settings.yml shows `embed_category: ''` being removed), so the INNER JOIN on `s.value = c.name` will return zero rows on default installs, making `[0]` nil and raising NoMethodError before the `if category_id == 0` uncategorized fallback can run — that fallback is indeed dead code. judged_text: `execute(...)[0]['id']` and `execute(...)[0]['value']` are indexed without a presence check, so when the first query returns no rows (embed_category setting absent, or its value not matching any category name exactly — e.g. the category was renamed or the setting stored an id), `[0]` is nil and the migration raises NoMethodError instead of reaching the `if category_id == 0` uncategorized fallback that was written for exactly this case. The migration crashes mid-run on affected installs (table already created, transaction not clean), blocking the deploy; and because the CREATE TABLE is not recorded, any re-run hits the force: true drop path. The uncategorized fallback branch at lines 13-15 is dead code — the crash always happens first when the join is empty.

adjudication.rationale: In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, `category_id = execute(...)[0]['id'].to_i` assumes the join query returns at least one row. If it returns zero rows (e.g., `embed_category` missing, or its `value` doesn’t match any `categories.name`), `execute(...)[0]` is `nil` and `nil['id']` raises before the `if category_id == 0` fallback can run. The same unchecked `[0]['value']` pattern is used for the uncategorized id lookup. This is a real, diff-grounded migration-crash risk.
